mbm-1701.clue: My easiest lift was the hardest one to start.
mbm-1701.quote: I hadn't been to the weight room for a year. My old gym partner put an empty bar on the rack and set a birthday candle in a cupcake beside it. We celebrated the first day back.

mbm-1702.clue: I know where to leave room for the laugh.
mbm-1702.quote: At our choro circle the flute player laughs just before the last run. The first time I caught that breath on my guitar she pointed straight at me. I nearly missed the last chord waving back.

mbm-1703.clue: My heels have a better memory than I do.
mbm-1703.quote: I copied our first waltz in chalk on the garage floor. A thin line stays under the tool chest. Every time we roll it out to change a tire I owe my wife one turn.

mbm-1704.clue: I measure my sunbaths in ferry crossings.
mbm-1704.quote: I stretch out on a striped towel at the sunny river beach. The deckhand waves on the way over. By the return trip I've rolled onto my stomach, so I wave back with one sandy foot.

mbm-1705.clue: Our youngest player invented a new currency.
mbm-1705.quote: My niece thought the little wooden roofs were cheese. We let her trade them for crackers. By the third round the red player owned a bakery and I owed her two slices of town hall.

mbm-1706.clue: I still have the leaf from my first call.
mbm-1706.quote: I built a wire aerial with my neighbor. A dry leaf blew into my notebook the instant we heard a voice across the harbor. We drew a line around it and wrote the call sign inside.

mbm-1707.clue: I save the quiet minute before the wheels touch.
mbm-1707.quote: From our spot at the airfield I can see a plane's shadow catch up with it on the runway. I tried to draw that once. The little gap between the wheels and my pencil line took all afternoon.

mbm-1708.clue: My museum ticket smells of lavender.
mbm-1708.quote: The guard near the tiny scent bottles handed me a sprig from the courtyard. I kept it in my ticket envelope. Three years later I can find that gallery just by opening the flap.

mbm-1709.clue: My radio log includes a soup recipe.
mbm-1709.quote: One wet Sunday my antenna picked up a neighbor describing his grandmother's soup. He read the ingredients as carefully as a call sign. Later we met at the market, both buying the same leeks.

mbm-1710.clue: I stitched the storm into the back.
mbm-1710.quote: My niece helped me pick sunny yellow pieces for a summer quilt while rain drummed on the roof. I worked a crooked line of blue stitching across the back. She calls it the sound side.

mbm-1711.clue: I count my steps with a children's rhyme.
mbm-1711.quote: Mum whispered a silly four-beat rhyme when she taught me to bowl. At league night she mouthed it from her seat. I left two pins standing and Mum held up two fingers. When I picked up the spare, we both shouted the last word.

mbm-1712.clue: I can recognize my king by its ear.
mbm-1712.quote: At our park table somebody chipped the crown of the black king. My opponent carved the nick into one pointy ear. Everybody else has a monarch. We have a cat who must be protected.

mbm-1713.clue: I set the clock by the pigeons.
mbm-1713.quote: Our chess table stands beneath a tree full of pigeons. I reached for my knight just as one dropped a twig onto its square. My opponent considered the position and offered the bird a draw.

mbm-1714.clue: I let the dog choose the channel on Fridays.
mbm-1714.quote: My daughter and I put the two program guides side by side. Whichever one the dog sleeps on wins. We watch a remarkable number of gardening shows in our pajamas that way.

mbm-1715.clue: I can read a request upside down.
mbm-1715.quote: Our DJ gives me the booth for ten minutes so he can dance to his own records. My friends write requests on their cuffs and lean over to show me. I can read a title upside down even with the lights flashing.

mbm-1716.clue: I wear the silver socks on the quiet bus home.
mbm-1716.quote: My friend couldn't hear my new dance step over the speakers. Outside, we watched our silver socks in the dark bus window and worked it out in perfect silence.

mbm-1717.clue: My books come with a time limit you can hear.
mbm-1717.quote: I read while Dad steams the breakfast buns. The lid rattles just as I reach the good part. On Sunday he put a second steamer on so I could finish the chapter.

mbm-1718.clue: I carry a tiny flag for the forbidden hole.
mbm-1718.quote: The course cat always naps inside the lighthouse. We made her a yellow paper flag and play the hole past her tail. Nobody's had the heart to ask for it back.

mbm-1719.clue: Our bass drum has a very soft job between gigs.
mbm-1719.quote: We rehearse in my uncle's tailor shop. Between songs he hangs a half-finished coat over the bass drum. The sleeves bounced in time during our last encore, and he left them there.

mbm-1720.clue: My best trick needs my sister's handwriting.
mbm-1720.quote: I ask someone to think of a fruit, then pull a tiny drawing from a lemon. My sister drew forty possibilities. The day someone chose lemon, I pulled out a portrait of the lemon wearing glasses.

mbm-1721.clue: I promised to leave one square wrinkled.
mbm-1721.quote: The nap of Grandad's corduroy jacket never lies flat. I put the elbow into a quilt square and kept the crease. Mum rests her hand there when she tells his fishing stories.

mbm-1722.clue: There's a return address sewn into the sea.
mbm-1722.quote: I sent my cousin half a quilted shoreline and she added the other shore. She stitched a tiny envelope into the waves with my house in red thread on the front.

mbm-1723.clue: I paint the same gate at a different hour.
mbm-1723.quote: The old gate looks gray if you hurry past. I've painted it at dawn, supper and in the rain. The owner held my three canvases together and asked where I'd hidden the fourth season.

mbm-1724.clue: My alarm clock has a very small violinist.
mbm-1724.quote: I wrote a program that puts a pixel musician on screen when it's time to practice. I gave him a chair so he can sit down when I run late. Sometimes he's asleep by the time I arrive.

mbm-1725.clue: I know the best patch of sun by the little bells.
mbm-1725.quote: I spread my towel near the harbor, just where I can hear the masts chime. When the shadow of the rail reaches my toes I pack up. The bells always get the last word.
